name: Polyunsaturated fat
what_is: Polyunsaturated fat is a type of fat whose fatty acids contain more than one double bond. The main families include omega-3 and omega-6 fatty acids.
why_botia: A nutrition label may declare polyunsaturated fat as one combined value without showing how much is omega-3 and how much is omega-6. BOTIA keeps that declared value separate from the regulatory information and evidence used to interpret it.
can_1: Read the polyunsaturated fat value when it is declared on the nutrition label and preserve its unit and basis.
can_2: Show that the value forms part of total fat rather than being added to it.
can_3: Connect the declared value with the applicable regulatory information and documented evidence where relevant.
cannot_1: Determine how much of the declared value is omega-3 and how much is omega-6 unless the label provides that breakdown.
cannot_2: Calculate polyunsaturated fat reliably from total fat and other declared fat values.
cannot_3: Treat polyunsaturated fat as equivalent to omega-3.
cannot_4: Treat an undeclared polyunsaturated fat value as zero.
